criteria.rationale: Examined the spec's L1 and L2 text. L1 discloses that implementer-written limits can be broad and requires the reviewer to challenge an unjustified limit; L2 binds edits to a new plan and bundle digest. Both assumptions are visible to this independent review, and L1 is an accepted human-review risk.

The accepted_limits and finding.limit fields are optional and omitted when empty, so existing records without limits keep their form. The new brief is versioned as review-brief/11; prior templates remain covered by the immutable-template integration evidence.
The change stays within pose-mcp and extends the shared attestation model. The integration assessment's three HTTP consumer gaps are unrelated to these changed contracts.
The digest fields use omitempty when no limits are present, and the tests preserve earlier brief versions. The change is additive for scopes without accepted limits.

The cause in the spec is repeated review rounds without a place to state the assumed environment. R1/R2 parse and seal those assumptions; D1 leaves semantic fit to the reviewer and records the sealed limit plus a reason; D2 makes edits stale the digest. The design assessment observed no structural delta.

Compared the English and Portuguese manuals with both embedded scaffold copies. Their accepted-limit behavior and review-brief/11 references match runtime; the brief renderer test also covers the new section.
R4 fails open on unreadable ADR inputs (N2); R3 also lacks a whitespace-trimmed reason check on the shared within-limit preflight (N1).
The changed behavior is confined to the accepted-limit parser, review plan and bundle, reviewer brief, attestation gate, ready-check, and matching docs/scaffold artifacts named by the spec.

Compared with prose-only limits, parsing and digest-sealing are the smallest sufficient way to keep later spec edits from changing the reviewed assumptions. Semantic inclusion remains reviewer judgment because automatic natural-language matching would be speculative; no round cap or model-based matcher is added. This choice would need revision if policy requires machine proof that each finding is contained in a limit. The shared preflight must still reject an empty reason.

findings.action: A whitespace-only rationale passes the within-limit preflight because the shared gate compares the field with the empty string. A structured signed attestation can therefore record a within-limit finding with no reason; require a trimmed non-empty rationale.

The ready check treats ADR directory read errors as no ADRs and skips unreadable ADR files. A present but unreadable ADR can therefore evade the required limit-reference check; fail closed on I/O errors while preserving the absent-directory case.
